Mawlana Pir Muzzaffar AhmadIslamic spiritual guide, Hadith scholar and educator

1927 – 2006 · Buthidaung, Arakan

ReligionEducation

A Rohingya Islamic scholar, Muhaddith and spiritual guide (Pir) from Mee Chaung Zay in Buthidaung Township, who devoted his life to teaching Hadith, Fiqh and the Qur'an, to spiritual guidance and to healing. He went to India for higher studies in 1947 and returned home in 1957; in 1977 the ulama of Arakan appointed him chairman of their committee with the title Khalifatul Muslimeen. Respected by Muslims across Arakan, he was also sought out for advice and treatment by many Buddhists and people of other faiths.

His story

A teacher and healer sought out across faiths

Mawlana Pir Muzzaffar Ahmad was a renowned Rohingya Islamic scholar, Muhaddith, and spiritual guide (Pir), known for his lifelong service to the Rohingya community through religious teaching, spiritual leadership, writing, social guidance, and healing. He was deeply respected by Muslims across Arakan and also admired by many Buddhists and people of other faiths who sought his advice and treatment. He was widely regarded as a rare scholar of strong character, a defender of oppressed people, a Deobandi-trained alim, and a senior spiritual successor (khalifah) connected to the tradition of Mawlana Husain Ahmad Madani.

He was born on 29 October 1927, in Mee Chaung Zay, Buthidaung Township. He began his studies in local Arabic and Urdu schools, including Mee Chaung Zay Arabic primary school (1934), an Urdu middle school in Hpon Nyo Leik village, and Paung Taw Pyin Madrasa (1940).

In June 1947, he traveled to India for higher studies. He returned home in February 1957 to serve his people and country. His life was dedicated to teaching Hadith, Fiqh, Qur’an, and spiritual purification. He was known as a clear and capable teacher, a healer for physical and spiritual suffering, and a guide for both scholars and ordinary people. He was skilled in Urdu, English, and Arabic, and recognized as a Muhaddith and spiritual Pir.

In 1971, he helped establish a religious organization in Bangladesh aimed at protecting Islamic teachings. He served as a central council leader in what became known as Khuddamul Islam and later Hemayatul Islam. In 1977, Arakan ulama formed a committee and appointed him as chairman, also granting him the title Khalifatul Muslimeen. Through these roles, he worked for the religious and social welfare of his community.

He authored two books: Jala’ al-Qulub, a work on Sufi spiritual training based on earlier classical texts, and Ishq Ahlian Burma, which documents oppression against Arakan people and serves as a historical record for future generations.

He was also associated with unity efforts around Burma’s independence era and was said to have signed agreements connected to cooperation among communities, believing Rohingya contributions to independence were often overlooked in official history.

Mawlana Pir Muzzaffar Ahmad passed away in 2006 after a lifetime of service. He is remembered as a major Rohingya alim, spiritual guide, teacher, writer, and community leader who dedicated his life to knowledge, faith, and the welfare of his people.
